cohort: Singleton pregnancies diagnosed with severe preeclampsia before 34 weeks gestation and without fetal growth restriction, managed at a large tertiary care center between January 2018 and January 2023.
finding: Abnormal umbilical artery Doppler waveforms in pregnancies with severe preeclampsia without fetal growth restriction were associated with earlier delivery (before 34 weeks gestation) and increased risk of neonatal complications, including respiratory distress syndrome.
mod_finding: Abnormal umbilical artery Doppler studies were associated with a decreased likelihood of vaginal delivery, and the absent end-diastolic flow subgroup had an increased likelihood of primary cesarean delivery.
gest_age: Severe preeclampsia diagnosed before 34 weeks gestation.
